cls: Hypomethylating agent / nucleoside metabolic inhibitor - antineoplastic
pharm: Pyrimidine nucleoside analogue of cytidine; DNA/RNA hypomethylating agent
quick: 75 mg/m2 daily for 7 days every 4 weeks (SC or IV); may increase to 100 mg/m2 after 2 cycles if no benefit and no toxicity
Can cause fetal harm; contraception required for both sexes during and after treatment
Do not breastfeed during and for 1 week after the last dose
Monitor closely; renal toxicity reported - hold/reduce for unexplained rises in BUN/creatinine
Contraindicated in advanced malignant hepatic tumors; higher toxicity risk in severe impairment
CBC (before each cycle), liver function, renal function and electrolytes (bicarbonate), pregnancy test
summary: Azacitidine (injectable) is a hypomethylating pyrimidine nucleoside analogue used to treat myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and related myeloid malignancies. Given subcutaneously or intravenously in 7-day cycles every 4 weeks, it causes DNA hypomethylation and cytotoxicity to abnormal marrow cells. Key risks are myelosuppression (anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia), hepatotoxicity, renal toxicity, and embryo-fetal harm. The injectable product must not be substituted for oral azacitidine.
indications: Adult patients with FAB myelodysplastic syndrome subtypes: refractory anemia (RA), RA with ringed sideroblasts (if accompanied by neutropenia/thrombocytopenia or requiring transfusions), refractory anemia with excess blasts (RAEB), RAEB in transformation (RAEB-T), and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML)

dosage.n: Premedicate for nausea/vomiting; same starting dose regardless of baseline counts
Increase only after at least 2 cycles if no benefit and no toxicity other than nausea/vomiting

dosage.d: Reduce dose or delay cycle per nadir counts / renal parameters
dosage.t: Adjust cycle timing and dose per label tables
dosage.n: Hold for serum bicarbonate <20 mEq/L or unexplained BUN/creatinine rise

admin: Reconstitute and administer subcutaneously or by IV infusion per the SC vs IV preparation instructions (they differ)
Rotate subcutaneous injection sites; SC suspension may be refrigerated within stability limits
Do NOT substitute injectable azacitidine for oral azacitidine - indications and dosing differ
Continue treatment as long as the patient benefits (at least 4-6 cycles recommended before judging response)
moa: Azacitidine is a pyrimidine nucleoside analogue of cytidine. It is believed to exert antineoplastic effects by causing hypomethylation of DNA (inhibiting DNA methyltransferase at low doses) and by direct cytotoxicity on abnormal hematopoietic cells in the bone marrow, restoring normal function to genes involved in differentiation and proliferation.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to azacitidine or to mannitol

preg: Based on mechanism of action and animal findings, azacitidine can cause fetal harm (teratogenic, embryotoxic). Advise effective contraception for females of reproductive potential during and after treatment, and for males with female partners of reproductive potential.
lact: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
renal: Monitor renal function. Renal toxicity (including renal failure, tubular acidosis) has been reported. Reduce dose or hold for unexplained reductions in serum bicarbonate (<20 mEq/L) or elevations of BUN/creatinine. Use caution in patients with renal impairment.
hepatic: Contraindicated in advanced malignant hepatic tumors. Patients with severe pre-existing hepatic impairment are at higher risk for hepatic toxicity (including progressive hepatic coma and death, particularly with extensive tumor burden and hypoalbuminemia). Use with caution.

minor: Drugs sharing the cytidine deaminase pathway (limited data)
interactions.diagnostics: CBC with differential and platelets before each cycle; liver function tests and serum creatinine/bicarbonate before therapy and as needed

monitoring: Complete blood count with differential and platelets before each dosing cycle and as indicated
Liver function tests and serum albumin before and during therapy
Renal function (BUN, creatinine) and serum electrolytes including bicarbonate
Pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential before treatment
Signs of infection, bleeding, and tumor lysis
counsel: This medicine is given as injections over 7 days, repeated about every 4 weeks
Expect low blood counts - report fever, sore throat, unusual bruising/bleeding, or signs of infection immediately
Nausea is common; anti-nausea medicine will be given
Use effective contraception (both partners) during and after treatment; do not breastfeed
Several cycles may be needed before benefit is seen
pk: Hematologic/clinical response typically after several cycles (often by cycle 4-6)
SC Tmax ~0.5 h; rapid distribution after IV
Unreconstituted vials at 25 C; reconstituted product use within stability limits (refrigerate SC suspension per label)
pearls: Do NOT confuse or substitute injectable azacitidine with ORAL azacitidine - indications and dosing differ and the products are not interchangeable.
Contraindicated in advanced malignant hepatic tumors and in mannitol hypersensitivity.
Give an adequate trial: at least 4-6 cycles (do not stop early) and only escalate to 100 mg/m2 after 2 cycles if no benefit and no significant non-GI toxicity.
Hold/reduce for unexplained drops in serum bicarbonate or rises in BUN/creatinine (renal toxicity signal).
missed: Doses are clinician-administered on a fixed cycle schedule; if a dose is missed or delayed, the oncology team adjusts the cycle. Patients should not attempt to self-administer or make up doses.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Overdose is associated with severe diarrhea, nausea/vomiting, and profound myelosuppression. Manage with supportive care, blood-count monitoring, transfusions/growth-factor support as needed, and treatment of infection.
